title: Stochastic Precision Fallback Orchestrator: reduce dequant overhead for mixed-precision serving
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We observe a 6–18% tail-latency regression on mixed-precision serving paths where requests cross precision boundaries (INT8 <-> FP8/FP16). Root cause analysis indicates excessive pointwise cast/dequant ops and fragmented kernel dispatch patterns that prevent kernel fusion and increase memory traffic during prefill and decode phases.

Proposal: Implement a Stochastic Precision Fallback Orchestrator (SPFO) that: 1) probes per-model and per-batch precision compatibility using low-cost microbenchmarks, 2) maintains a short-lived precision-affinity cache keyed by (model, route, seq_len_bucket), 3) applies probabilistic fallback rules to prefer quant-friendly fused kernels and amortize dequant casts across microbatches, and 4) provides a runtime hint to the kernel selector to enable cheap in-kernel requantization paths instead of performing expensive host-side dequant/cast.

Goals: Reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead from dequant/cast by 20–40% on mixed workloads, lower 95th percentile latency by at least 10% on affected routes, and keep aggregate output quality delta < 0.5% (task-level metric) compared to baseline precision-aware path.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark showing >=20% reduction in dequant-related GPU time on mixed INT8/FP8 workloads
95p latency for sampled production routes improves by >=10% compared to current mixed-precision baseline
No regression in correctness: model outputs measured on our eval prompt set show <0.5% change in key quality metrics
Feature gated with server flag and rollout circuit that can be toggled per-customer or per-route
Automated unit and integration tests covering precision-affinity cache expiry, fallback probability jitter, and kernel-selector hints
implementation_notes: Phase 1: low-risk probing + cache (week 1-2) - add a microbenchmark runner that executes 16-token warmup slices through INT8 and FP8 fused kernels on a sampled trace; store latency/cost delta. Phase 2: orchestrator + kernel hint (week 2-4) - implement SPFO state machine that updates precision-affinity cache and emits a kernel_selector_hint with preferred path and max_fallbacks. Phase 3: in-kernel support + reclamation (week 4-6) - coordinate with kernel team to enable in-kernel requantization fast-path; add eviction and telemetry rollups. Phase 4: rollout and kill-switch (week 6-8) - gated canary, A/B with auto-rollback on error budget burn. Use feature flag 'spfo_enabled'.
test_plan: Microbench harness: comparative run of fused kernels vs baseline with and without SPFO enabled
Simulated traffic: replay 24h of representative mixed-precision traces and assert latency and token cost improvements
Regression evals: run eval-suite for NLG tasks to detect quality drift
Stress tests: long-run stability with frequent fallback flips and affinity-cache churn
Canary: 1% hosts -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring thresholds for rollback
rollout_plan: Deploy SPFO as opt-in behind feature flag to dedicated staging cluster
Run synthetic load and internal canary against production-like models for 48h
Enable 1% traffic in hosted control plane; monitor token-level cost and 95p latency for 48h
Incrementally increase to 10% and 50% with manual checkpoints and rollback gates
Full enable with metrics verified and announcement to SRE/Support teams
